extracted.intended_audience: nonbank covered persons, compliance officers, regulated entities, and regulatory counsel interacting with CFPB rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements (and the CFPB's reasoning for rescinding them) governing registration, reporting, publication, and related compliance obligations for nonbank covered persons subject to certain agency and court orders under 12 CFR part 1092.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covered nonbank registration requirement (§1092.202)
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered nonbanks that are subject to certain public agency and court orders related to offering or providing a consumer financial product or service must register with the Bureau and submit required information about each covered order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration applies to covered orders in effect as of specified implementation dates or that take effect thereafter. The rule enumerates who qualifies as a covered nonbank and which orders are 'covered orders.' Registration is the predicate for other reporting and potential publication provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required registration data elements (§1092.202(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: At registration, a covered nonbank must submit: (1) a fully executed, accurate, and complete copy of the covered order (public portions only), and information identifying (i) agency(ies)/court(s) issuing the order, (ii) effective date, (iii) expiration date or statement of none, (iv) all covered laws found or alleged to have been violated, and (v) any docket/case/tracking numbers assigned to the order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonpublic portions of orders must not be submitted and must be clearly marked on the copy submitted. Registrants must follow Bureau filing instructions and submit identifying and administrative information as defined in the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission format and marking of nonpublic information
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of covered orders must be submitted in the Bureau-specified format, and any nonpublic portions of an order must be excluded from submission and clearly marked on the copy provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants must follow the CFPB Nonbank Registration Filing Instructions Guide and any technical filing instructions for the data intake system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative registration pathway for NMLS-published covered orders (§1092.203(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a covered order is published on the NMLS Consumer Access website, a covered nonbank may satisfy the registration requirement by submitting limited identifying information referencing the NMLS-published order instead of the full registration data described in §1092.202.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under this alternative, there is no requirement to provide ongoing updates. Filing instructions specify the limited information to provide (e.g., effective date, identifying number, explanation of differences if any).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing update and correction obligations (§1092.202(f) & §1092.205(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must submit updated information regarding the status of a covered order on an ongoing basis and must file corrections within 30 days after becoming aware or having reason to know of an inaccuracy in prior submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include filings within 90 days after termination, modification, abrogation, or ceasing to be a covered order. Corrections and updates are mandatory as specified in the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and implementation deadlines (registration within 90 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration is required within 90 days after the applicable nonbank registry implementation date, or 90 days after the effective date of the covered order, whichever is later. The rule sets phased implementation dates for different categories of registrants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation dates included: Oct 16, 2024 (larger participants supervised registrants), Jan 14, 2025 (other supervised registrants), and Apr 14, 2025 (all other covered nonbanks), producing corresponding registration deadlines in 2025 per the rule text and filing guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual covered-order reporting for Bureau-supervised registered entities (§1092.204)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supervised registered entities (subject to specified thresholds/exclusions) must submit an annual written statement describing the steps an attesting executive undertook to oversee activities subject to the covered order during the preceding calendar year and must attest whether, to their knowledge, any violations or noncompliance occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual reporting requirements apply to orders not registered via NMLS and to supervised registrants meeting the rule's size/coverage criteria. The written statement must be signed by the attesting executive and include specified information per §1092.204(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation and role of an attesting executive (§1092.204(b)-(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A supervised registered entity must designate an attesting executive for each covered order and must provide that executive access to required documents and information necessary to make the annual written statement and attestation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The attesting executive's name and title may be published; the Bureau's prior notices discussed potential publication of the identity of the attesting executive and related operational considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential legal liability for written statements (criminal false statement concerns)
rubrics_metrics.description: The written-statement requirement implicates potential liability under 18 U.S.C. 1001 for false statements, and the Bureau noted commenters' concerns about lack of explicit mens rea language in the NBR Rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bureau referenced executive orders and policy guidance that agencies should explicitly state conduct subject to criminal enforcement and applicable mens rea standards when a regulation could carry criminal consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication authority and limits (§1092.205)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bureau is authorized to make available to the public (on its website) information submitted to the nonbank registry other than administrative information, and to publish aggregate information collected under the registration and annual reporting requirements, but publication is discretionary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NBR Rule stated the Bureau intends to publish information but reserved the option not to publish based on operational constraints; published information could include the identity of attesting executives subject to specified limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of 'covered order' and temporal coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule's definition of 'covered order' includes orders with an effective date on or later than January 1, 2017 (along with other definitional criteria), subject to additional exclusions and specifications in §1092.201.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix A to §1092 listed State laws considered 'covered law' for purposes of the definition. The NBR Rule also described the types of orders (agency and court orders under various Federal and State provisions) that trigger registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of 'covered person' and exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'covered person' universe for registration excludes insured depository institutions, insured credit unions, certain motor vehicle dealers, natural persons, federally recognized Tribes, and persons subject to enumerated exclusions in CFPA section 1027; it otherwise targets nonbank covered persons offering or providing consumer financial products or services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule and accompanying definitions in §1092.201 specify covered nonbank categories and explicitly state excluded classes; commenters raised objections about inclusion of certain affiliates and CUSOs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork burden and cost estimates (agency PRA analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB supporting statements estimated paperwork burdens (e.g., 5 hours for initial registration, 30 hours for first annual report including recordkeeping; aggregate burdens in excess of 271,000 hours) and per-order labor cost estimates ($350 initial registration; $2,100 annual report for supervised registrant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Bureau also estimated federal government costs to operate the registry (approx. $2.5M external vendor support and 10,400 staff hours) and personnel needs (five full-time employees) in supporting the system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of reporting obligation (annual reporting timeframe)
rubrics_metrics.description: The NBR Rule requires annual reporting for covered orders for at least a 10-year period (the annual reporting cycle persists for 10 years from registration as described in the rule).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimated burdens in the NBR Rule accounted for multiple reporting cycles; commenters highlighted the long duration as a cost driver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction timeframe for inaccurate submissions (30-day rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered entities must file corrections within 30 days after becoming aware or having reason to know of an inaccuracy in their prior submissions to the registry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement is explicit in the NBR Rule and applies to both registration data and other submissions required under the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional good-faith filings asserting non-applicability (§1092.202(g) & §1092.204(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule provides a non-mandatory mechanism for persons to submit filings indicating a good-faith basis to believe the NBR Rule or one or more provisions does not apply to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These optional filings are not mandatory information collection requirements and were identified but not discussed in depth in the final rule preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: CFPA section 1022(b) rulemaking consideration standard
rubrics_metrics.description: When promulgating rules under CFPA section 1022(b), the Bureau must consider potential benefits and costs of the regulation to consumers and covered persons, including potential reduction in access to consumer financial products and services, impacts on insured depository institutions/credit unions under $10B in assets, and impacts on consumers in rural areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statutory standard guided the Bureau's evaluation of the NBR Rule and the Proposed Rescission Rule; the Bureau cited the absence of non-speculative, methodologically rigorous support for claimed benefits as a reason to rescind.

rubrics_metrics.name: CFPA §1024(b)(2) supervisory prioritization factors
rubrics_metrics.description: For supervisory decisions under CFPA section 1024(b)(1)-(2), the Bureau must take into account: (A) asset size of the covered person, (B) volume of transactions involving consumer financial products/services, (C) risks to consumers created by provision of those products/services, (D) extent of State oversight for consumer protection, and (E) any other factors the Bureau determines relevant to a class of covered persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These factors inform the Bureau's use of information (including whether a registry is necessary) for risk-based supervision and examinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplication/coordination consideration (interaction with NMLS and other sources)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency must consider whether the Bureau's registry duplicates existing public databases (e.g., NMLS, State and Federal regulator websites, legal/regulatory databases) and whether centralization provides unique, non-duplicative benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters argued registry was duplicative; Bureau agreed duplication and availability of public orders elsewhere weighed against the rule's utility in addressing recidivism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeting precision for recidivism-monitoring (overbreadth concern)
rubrics_metrics.description: A valid rule aimed at addressing recidivism should focus on repeat offenders rather than requiring registration for entities with a single order or for orders not reflecting liability; overbroad scope undermines targeted monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Bureau concluded NBR Rule was overbroad (e.g., requiring registration for single orders and for orders without admission/denial of liability) and therefore did not effectively address recidivism relative to its burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescission and severability approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Rescission of the registration requirements necessarily results in rescission of the written-statement and publication provisions because those components are predicated on registration; partial rescission (registration only) was not considered a reasonable alternative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Bureau therefore finalized rescission of 12 CFR part 1092 in its entirety as applied to the NBR Rule's components and rendered certain sections removed and reserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency discretion to publish or not publish collected data
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the Bureau authorized publication of non-administrative registration information and aggregate reporting data, the publication provisions do not compel the Bureau to publish and permit operational considerations (e.g., resource constraints) to limit publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NBR Rule stated the Bureau's intent to publish but specifically reserved the right not to publish certain information for operational reasons.
